stem: For a small configuration increment δq, which statement connects the Jacobian to position changes?

options.text: δx=J (q)δq is exact for every finite increment of any nonlinear map
The Jacobian multiplies only positions, never rates
The Jacobian is independent of q for every map
δx≈J (q)δq is a local first-order approximation; the velocity relation is instantaneous

solution.justification: A derivative gives the local linear part; nonlinear maps have higher-order terms for finite changes.

optionExplanations.o1: Correct. A derivative gives the local linear part; nonlinear maps have higher-order terms for finite changes.
optionExplanations.o2: Incorrect. The omitted higher-order terms generally matter for finite increments.
optionExplanations.o3: Incorrect. The source uses J to map joint rates.
optionExplanations.o4: Incorrect. The partial derivatives can change with configuration.
